description: Active RedCap Evolution Factory candidates. Keep this file concise; archive or promote handled candidates instead of letting it become a second lessons.md.

candidates.problem_source: The user repeatedly asked for lessons and identity sedimentation to be automatic, but RedCap previously implemented only local visibility checks and author-reminder gates.
candidates.solution: Introduce an Evolution Factory candidate flow so high-value experience, identity, skill, rule, and governance findings must be captured as candidates before promotion or explicit no-promote closure.
candidates.final_effect: Future closeout can reason about concrete candidates instead of relying on the author to remember whether something should be sedimented.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Connect candidate checks to diagnose/spec-check now, then connect strict unresolved-candidate blocking to closeout before declaring R6 complete.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This candidate flow handles RedCap-owned closeout and diagnostic surfaces; live per-message capture remains host-limited without a host pre-reply hook.

candidates.problem_source: Cap identity growth was treated like a normal lesson update in earlier discussions, but active identity content is personal memory and should not be mutated by a background agent.
candidates.solution: Route personality-growth signals into identity candidates first; promotion may produce an identity proposal, but active identity.md must not be auto-edited without explicit review.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can avoid losing personality-growth signals while still protecting the identity anchor from automatic corruption.
candidates.recurrence_guard: The candidate schema declares identity candidates as proposal-only by default, and the Evolution-grade baseline keeps identity sedimentation manual-only until reviewed promotion exists.
candidates.applicability_boundary: Automatic discovery is allowed; automatic active identity mutation is not allowed.

candidates.problem_source: A temporary Copilot CLI freeze could be written into routing or health surfaces while launchers still retained direct execution paths.
candidates.solution: Promote provider freeze to a machine-readable provider policy consumed by health probes, reviewer ordering, stop-review execution, baton launching, agent detection, and Prism dispatch checks.
candidates.final_effect: Frozen providers are blocked at RedCap-owned launch points, and missing policy data fails closed for Copilot-sensitive paths.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Acceptance now covers live-health freeze, missing-policy health probing, baton rejection, detect-agents freeze reporting, and Prism roster rejection.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This governs RedCap-owned launch paths; historical report text and user-run manual shell commands remain outside repository enforcement.

candidates.problem_source: The user needed a human-readable grasp of key machine files, but adding long explanations to every file would risk recreating context bloat.
candidates.solution: Create a concise lookup dictionary as the primary explanation surface, then add short dictionary backlinks only where useful.
candidates.final_effect: Humans and Agents can locate file intent without loading large docs or duplicating long comments across JSON and scripts.
candidates.recurrence_guard: CONTRIBUTING.core and README now route file-meaning questions to the dictionary instead of expanding large rule files by default.
candidates.applicability_boundary: The dictionary explains stable control files; volatile run evidence should remain in ignored run-scoped storage and be summarized only when promoted.

candidates.problem_source: The user observed that a six-hour RedCap task produced only a route-level outcome while the intended system-level restructuring was broader.
candidates.solution: Add an original-intent coverage gate to PM Gate so task cards must declare scope_status, covered intent, uncovered/deferred scope, human-visible boundaries, and follow-up paths before execution and closeout.
candidates.final_effect: Future receipts and promise ledgers can no longer prove only a silently narrowed task without also surfacing whether the user's original strategic intent was fully implemented, route-only, or partially deferred.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-intent-coverage-check.sh is consumed by PM Gate and diagnose, with acceptance fixtures covering both a valid partial-defer case and a missing coverage section.
candidates.applicability_boundary: The gate makes scope narrowing visible and machine-blocked when omitted; it does not make natural-language semantic coverage perfect without Prism planning review or human strategic input.

candidates.problem_source: Layer B closeout reached the notification gate, but the configured lark-cli direct-message transport was blocked by a local profile/scope mismatch, so receipt generation could not complete even though validator-chain had passed.
candidates.solution: Add a webhook notify-only transport to feishu-notifier.py so completion notifications can still be sent when bidirectional lark-cli windows are unavailable.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can keep completion notification visible while honestly marking webhook followup as one-way and not pretending ask/resume is available.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Acceptance now covers webhook followup degradation and verifies that the notification payload is sent without creating a reply window.
candidates.applicability_boundary: Webhook transport is single-direction only; interactive ask/resume/confirm still require lark_cli_dm with valid scopes.

candidates.problem_source: The user explicitly required Prism to stop wasting long-task time on unavailable Agent CLIs and to maintain a one-hour availability list before each Prism use.
candidates.solution: Introduce prism-availability as a TTL cache and roster gate, require provider-qualified roster specs, wire the gate into prism-dispatch-check, and cover it with acceptance plus execution guarantees.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap-owned Prism dispatch now rejects unavailable, frozen, timed-out, unsupported, or provider-unqualified rosters before launch instead of discovering the failure after delegation stalls.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-spec-check, redcap-diagnose, prism-dispatch-check, and the prism-availability acceptance case keep the TTL cache path visible and tested.
candidates.applicability_boundary: The cache proves current local provider availability, not model suitability; model selection still depends on capability matrix, task risk, and Prism role design.

candidates.problem_source: The user challenged whether RedCap's reports, lessons, identity growth, and shared methods should continue living inside the skill-root execution layer and risk recreating a token sink.
candidates.solution: Add a shared-knowledge repository template with per-user namespaces, append-only timestamped entries, index-first retrieval, exact duplicate rejection, and an explicit remote-binding boundary.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can start treating team memory as an external shared layer while keeping the current execution layer lean and preserving a safe migration path for future Gitee binding.
candidates.recurrence_guard: shared-knowledge policy, check script, file dictionary coverage, spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance now protect the local template and append-only behavior.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This is the local repository shape and tooling; remote Gitee creation, permissions, and historical asset physical migration remain explicit follow-up work.

candidates.problem_source: The user observed that interim terminal reports lacked a stable status surface and Feishu repeatedly sent Layer B audit-failure notifications, making it hard to distinguish node reports from internal control-plane noise.
candidates.solution: Promote human-facing status updates to a policy-backed surface, add a formatter and validator, align Feishu report formatting to the same fields, and mute SessionEnd / Stop internal audit-gap Feishu sends by default while preserving pending closure and diagnostics.
candidates.final_effect: Future checkpoints and Feishu node reports expose whether Norven must act, whether the task is blocked, whether the next step can start, the task panorama, and the current node; internal audit gaps stay in ledger/diagnostics unless explicitly escalated as true manual intervention.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-human-communication-check.sh, redcap-feishu-notification-policy-check.sh, spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance case human-communication-check validate the surface and notification-noise boundary.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This governs RedCap-owned terminal formatter, Feishu formatter, SessionEnd, and legacy Stop hook paths; it cannot rewrite historical Feishu messages already sent.

candidates.problem_source: P4-2a pre-release review showed that npm pack, package safety and clean-workspace E2E can pass while RedCap is still not a public-release-ready CLI/runtime product. Prism also found path-leak and checker self-cycle risks in the first implementation.
candidates.solution: Promote a separate pre-release product architecture gate that judges privacy, machine independence, CLI product quality, source visibility, public knowledge claims and distribution compliance before public release readiness or npm publish.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can now truthfully say P4-2a judgment is complete while blocking public release behind explicit product architecture blockers, instead of confusing package generation with product readiness.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-pre-release-product-architecture-check.sh, spec-check, diagnose and targeted acceptance require the blocker ledger to match actual package, CLI, split and redcap-arsenal facts.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This gate judges and blocks release readiness; it does not by itself remediate the identified runtime split, CLI doctor/debug/trace, package identity/license or public-arsenal content gaps.

candidates.problem_source: The information architecture task showed that RedCap reports, private knowledge, runtime evidence, shared templates and public arsenal candidates could be confused under broad docs/knowledge wording. Prism also identified that report-led live summaries are a host-limited natural-language surface and should not be claimed as fully deterministic without explicit boundary registration.
candidates.solution: Promote an information architecture governance policy plus RedCap Forge policy: classify assets by lifecycle and export boundary, forbid raw private sources from public arsenal, require report-led human summaries, and register the new boundaries in execution guarantees with honest manual-only wording where live reply control is host-limited.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can preserve archaeology and task tracking while reducing token-sprawl, private-content leakage risk, and report/arsenal confusion. Future public knowledge entries must pass through RedCap Forge instead of directly copying raw reports or runtime traces.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-information-architecture-check.sh, redcap-forge-check.sh, redcap-human-communication-check.sh, execution-guarantees check, spec-check, diagnose and targeted acceptance validate the boundaries.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This lesson governs information architecture and public-promotion boundaries. It does not migrate historical private content into redcap-arsenal or make every host live reply physically vetoable.
